units.content: Proposed changes are classified as metadata, experimental successor work, implementation/benchmark work, or architectural reopening.
THESIS, ARCHITECTURE, GOVERNANCE and BENCHMARK are expected unchanged unless a reopening condition and discriminating evidence are supplied.
Change proposals must justify why the revision is the shallowest and smallest sufficient change.
Proposals must state checks, remaining uncertainty, and evidence that would narrow, revert or supersede the change.
Version 1.0.0 is recorded as frozen candidate architecture on 2026-08-06.

Release summary includes authority-bearing updates, learning/adaptation distinctions, ecology, arbitration, challenge/integrity, constitutional debt, four-class benchmark, minimal sufficient revision, support/failure/break statuses, and empirical stop rule.
Controlled Adaptation v1.0 is declared frozen at commit 91ffe403879607d40a5e9c8babed1c5016ba0eba on 2026-08-06 and empirically unvalidated.
Core v1.0 files are THESIS.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/GOVERNANCE.md and docs/BENCHMARK.md.
Git comparison from freeze commit to current head shows one post-freeze commit and zero changes to the four declared core files.
README, STATUS, CHANGELOG, LINEAGE and contribution/review templates may change repository-state metadata without rewriting v1.0.
Metadata must distinguish freeze-time claims, later successor hypotheses, and evidence actually produced.

Successor distinction promotion requires recurrent unrepresentable failure, independent replication, successful successor resolution, failure of simpler revisions, and benefit exceeding representation/governance cost.
A new distinction cannot inherit architectural authority merely because it explains the frozen structure elegantly.
Later research is related to Controlled Adaptation v1.0 by conceptual lineage, not automatic authority inheritance.
Causal Mass is named as conceptual ancestor and counterfactual measurement hypothesis, but no primary Causal Mass artifact is present in R36 to bind or independently verify the referent.
Counterfactual difference-making is stated not to determine value, causal responsibility or warranted authority by itself.
Consequence-to-Authority Bridge v0.1 is named as experimental successor hypothesis with benchmark authority but no architectural inheritance; its primary artifact is absent from R36.
Bridge conversion is reported as causal difference→evaluative significance→identified responsibility→typed targeted scoped authority change, with candidate chain Y−Ŷ→𝒟→(𝒱,ℐ)→𝒯_A→ΔA_{τ,j}(s,h,c).
Controlled Adaptation v1.0 is frozen, conceptually specified and empirically unvalidated; it governs authority-bearing structure after an admissible update is formed.

A separate Constitutional Continual Adaptation Benchmark v0.1 preregistration is reported frozen with SHA-256 45a3594cf43ca73817082a667a63e1095113f45f70337ec00b81f46836e386f0, but that primary preregistration artifact is absent from R36.
Reported benchmark authority is limited to test interpretation and cannot redefine the frozen core or prove ontology by construction.

Successful ancestor formalization does not imply bridge mechanism; bridge success does not imply core reopening; architecture coherence does not validate ancestor; performance does not imply ontology; conceptual fit does not imply mechanism; mechanism evidence does not rewrite history.
A 'self-governance event' is reported as one local procedural consistency result, but no primary event artifact or execution record is present in R36 to independently inspect it.
Theory is frozen; bridge is frozen as hypothesis; evaluation is frozen as protocol; experiment is said to begin with evaluator validation.
Repository routes readers to v1.0 as a frozen candidate architecture of authority-bearing structure.
README identifies freeze commit 91ffe403... and states successor concepts may shape experiments without architectural authority.
Current status is coherent candidate architecture, not validated theory; next authority increase requires adversarial testing against simpler baselines.
README reports conceptual sequence Causal Mass→Bridge v0.1→Controlled Adaptation v1.0→Benchmark v0.1; this is source lineage, not resolved Cerebro topology.
First implementation milestone is benchmark validity: causal hidden loci, concealment before diagnostic evidence, recoverability after valid evidence, and intervention-grounded scoring oracle.
v1.0 remains conceptually specified and empirically unvalidated and has not demonstrated superiority over simpler correction, memory, arbitration or continual-learning mechanisms.
Source assigns bounded roles to Causal Mass, v1.0, Bridge v0.1 and Benchmark v0.1 and states no object automatically inherits authority from another.

Supported conceptual distinctions include content vs authority-bearing update; governed update vs update governance; calibration vs learning; learning vs adaptation; failure loci; authority removal vs lineage erasure; corrigibility vs steerability; minimal vs minimal sufficient revision.
Bridge remains experimental only, outside v1.0, and may be supported, narrowed, superseded or defeated by future benchmark evidence.

Open questions include authority-envelope utility, causal localization, constitutional revision, challenge selectivity, ecology scaling, layer necessity, behavioral recovery prediction, bridge comparison, mediation and generator validity.

Next authorized work is evaluator-validity implementation: latent generators, matched renderers, intervention-grounded oracles, leakage/independence audits, and a frozen validity result set before agent comparison; none is implemented in R36 head.

Core reopening requires unrepresentable necessary distinction, indistinguishable frozen layers, failed predicted governance operator, materially simpler explanatory alternative, or systematic challenge failure outside frozen representational capacity; implementation/local/bridge/benchmark outcomes alone do not automatically reopen core.
